subject: Learning Methods
title: The Book-to-Notes Pipeline
description: A quick win: understand The Book-to-Notes Pipeline.

hook.text: Ryan Holiday keeps a box of index cards, one per idea from each book he reads.

buildup.text: A book-to-notes pipeline captures key ideas during reading and stores them for future use and review.

discovery.text: After finishing a chapter, write the top three ideas on separate cards or notes. One idea per note forces clarity.

twist.text: More notes is not better. Selecting the few ideas worth keeping requires judgment that itself deepens understanding.

climax.text: Build a simple system: read, select key ideas, write them in your words, and review monthly.

punchline.text: Capture less, in your own words. Quality beats quantity.

quiz.question: Why does writing one idea per note force clarity?
options: It saves space on each card
Selecting the few ideas worth keeping requires judgment that deepens understanding
Multiple ideas per note are harder to organize alphabetically
